analysis.title: CoreWeave Inc: Execution and Structural Pricing Tailwinds Could Ease AI Funding Concerns
key_insights: RJ keeps Outperform and a $75 12M target on CRWV (price $48.73 as of Nov-10-26). It says investors underappreciate CoreWeave's path to a top-tier hyperscaler with 8GW of critical IT power ambitions by 2030.
3Q26 revenue was $3.7B (+168% y/y), ahead of Street at $3.6B. Adjusted EBIT margin was 10.4% vs Street 6.9% and RJe 6.5%.
GPU pricing rose ~25% in July and a further ~10% later in 3Q, with additional 4Q gains exceeding cost inflation. Ampere/Hopper pricing rose 30-50% q/q.
Short-term contracts command >$40M in annual revenue per MW vs $20-25M for four- to five-year contracts. Payback on long-dated contracts is shrinking to one to two years from two to three years.

About 130K GPUs roll off contract in 2027 and ~170K more in 2028. CoreWeave sizes annualized recontracting at nearly $4B for the 2027 cohort and nearly $10B across both cohorts, with no incremental GPU capex.

Funding visibility is improving: ~$9B of customer prepayments and deposits expected over the next three months, ~$9B of construction-in-progress, ~$5B of undrawn DDTLs, and a new DDTL expected to finance at 7-7.5% with >90% financing of associated capex.

RJ models operating cash flow of $7.5B in 2026 vs $3B in 2025 (the report's own OCF estimate table shows $9.07B for 2026, so the two figures differ within the note). RJ considers $5B of parent-level financing a reasonable starting point for 2027, with a 35M share ATM authorized as a smaller contributor.
Weighted-average debt cost fell 250 bp y/y to 7.9%. Investment-grade and enterprise customers account for >75% of remaining committed 2027 capex not already attached to a DDTL.
Active power rose >200MW in 3Q to >1.7GW across 52 data centers, with the >1.85GW year-end target maintained. Contracted power rose >900MW to >4.6GW, including >1.3GW internationally.
Backlog was $132.5B (+138% y/y), about 6% above RJe ($125.5B) and 1% above Street ($131.1B).
Capex of $14.5B exceeded RJe/Street of $12.5B as customer deployments accelerated. 2026 capex guidance narrowed to $37-39B from $35-39B.
2026 revenue guidance rose to $13.0-13.3B, exit ARR guidance to $20-21B, and adj. EBIT guidance to $1.275-1.375B (up 26% at the midpoint).

CoreWeave sees qualified demand at ~10x available capacity through 2027. Customers committing >$100M grew >2.5x y/y, and industries outside AI labs and tech were more than half of new customers this year.

Managed inference passed $250M of booked ARR, reaching its year-end target early. Forge users were 70% of new 3Q cloud customers. Omni lets customers run CoreWeave's platform on infrastructure they own, and one customer has signed.
CoreWeave brought Vera Rubin into production with Cognition, achieving 4.8x GB200 token throughput on its workloads.
RJ scenario values are $75 base, $125 bull and $25 bear, against $48.73 current. The base case rests on 10x 2028E EV/EBIT, toward the middle of hyperscaler peers (AMZN, ORCL, DOCN).

market_movers.rationale: Pricing gains, operating profit upside and improving funding visibility ease funding concerns. RJ keeps the $75 target on 10x 2028E EV/EBIT.

sector_views.rationale: Qualified demand is ~10x available capacity through 2027, and GPU pricing is rising with recontracting upside at no incremental GPU capex.

earnings_insights: CRWV 3Q26 reported revenue $3,661M (+168% y/y) vs Street est $3,557M and RJ est $3,525M.
CRWV 3Q26 reported adj. (non-GAAP) operating income $379M, 10.4% margin, vs Street est $245M (6.9%) and RJ est $230M (6.5%).
CRWV 3Q26 reported non-GAAP EPS ($0.95) vs Street est ($1.20) and RJ est ($1.41). Reported GAAP EPS ($1.27) vs Street est ($1.49) and RJ est ($1.78).
CRWV 3Q26 reported backlog (adj. RPO) $132.5B (+138% y/y) vs Street est $131.1B and RJ est $125.5B.
CRWV 3Q26 reported capex $14,511M vs Street est $12,459M and RJ est $12,500M. Reported FCF (CFO less capex) was ($12,536M) vs Street est ($9,239M).
CRWV 3Q26 reported exit ARR $14,644M vs Street est $14,229M and RJ est $14,100M. Non-GAAP gross margin was 67.8% vs Street est 67.0%.
Company guidance (reported 11/10-11/11): 2026 revenue $13.0-13.3B, exit ARR $20-21B, adj. EBIT $1.275-1.375B, capex $37-39B, year-end active power >1.85GW.

RJ estimate changes: 2026/2027 revenue to $13.2B/$26.6B from $12.8B/$25.5B. Adj. EBIT to $1.33B/$4.00B from $1.06B/$3.38B. Capex to $38B/$46B from $37B/$46B. OCF to $9.07B/$18.96B from $9.36B/$20.23B.

trade_ideas.rationale: Pricing tailwinds, operating profit upside and improving funding visibility, with recontracting upside from GPUs rolling off in 2027 and 2028.
trade_ideas.risk: Funding needs: RJ estimates financing needs of ($36.6B) in 2026 and ($38.0B) in 2027, and 2026/2027 FCF of ($28.9B)/($27.0B). Parent-level financing, including the ATM, could dilute shareholders.

risk_factors: Funding: RJ estimates financing needs of ($36.6B) for 2026 and ($38.0B) for 2027, with FCF of ($28.9B)/($27.0B).
Parent-level capital: RJ assumes ~$5B for 2027, and a 35M share ATM is authorized.
Capex overruns: 3Q capex was $14.5B vs Street $12.5B, and RJ raises its 2026 capex estimate to $38B.
Margin dilution: non-GAAP gross margin was 67.8% in 3Q26, down 5.5 points y/y.
RJ's bear case values the stock at $25, 52% below the current price. The 52-week range is $40.58-$138.25.

tension_points.bull_case: Customer prepayments (~$9B), ~$9B of construction-in-progress, ~$5B undrawn DDTL, a new DDTL at 7-7.5% and rising OCF leave only a modest ~$5B parent-level need in 2027, per RJ.
tension_points.bear_case: RJ estimates FCF of ($28.9B) in 2026 and ($27.0B) in 2027 and financing needs of ($36.6B) and ($38.0B), with $5.8B of equity/converts in 2027 and a 35M share ATM authorized. RJ's bear case is $25 per share.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Parent-level financing materially above the ~$5B RJ assumes for 2027, or customer prepayments falling short of the ~$9B expected over the next three months.

theme_stances.key_argument: Robust execution and an accommodating pricing environment led to operating profit upside, potentially easing concerns amid a cautious AI funding backdrop.
theme_stances.evidence: investors underappreciate the opportunity for CoreWeave to develop into a top-tier hyperscaler
